answer: Each identity holds one slot on the mesa registry, marked by a saffron tag stating its price. The owner locks 200 credits and pays a tide tax of 10 percent of that price each tide, so one honest identity pays 20 credits per tide and keeps its slot. Anyone may buy a slot at its tagged price and evict the holder, so a cheap fake is bought out at once. The kth fake still pays 200 plus 20 per tide, so 1,000 fakes lock 200,000 credits and pay 20,000 per tide, with no bulk discount. A rented tag fails because the registry checks signer against owner and burns the bond on mismatch.
